questions.text:
Consider a RISC machine where each instruction is exactly 4 bytes long. Conditional and unconditional branch instructions use PC- relative addressing mode with Offset specified in bytes to the target location of the branch instruction. Further the Offset is always with respect to the address of the next instruction in the program sequence. Consider the following instruction sequence.

If the target of the branch instruction is i, then the decimal value of the Offset is __________
questions.solution:
The offset is measured from the instruction after the branch, i.e. i + 4 (in instruction numbers). The target is i, which is 4 instructions back.

Offset = [latex]-[/latex]4 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 bytes = [latex]-[/latex]16

Answer: -16

questions.text: Relative mode of addressing is most relevant to writing:
questions.solution:
Relative (PC-relative) addressing gives addresses as an offset from the current instruction, so the code works wherever it is loaded: position-independent code.

Answer: Position - independent code

questions.text:
For computers based on three-address instruction formats, each address field can be used to specify which of the following:
(S1) A memory operand
(S2) A processor register
(S3) An implied accumulator register
questions.solution:
In a three-address instruction, each address field explicitly names a memory location or a register. An implied accumulator is used only in one-address formats.

Answer: Either S1 or S2

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: All of S1, S2 and S3

questions.text: MOV [BX], AL  type of data addressing is called ?
questions.solution:
[BX] means "the memory location whose address is in BX". The operand's address comes from a register, which is register indirect addressing.

Answer: register indirect
